paper.abstract_en: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.
